I need the Moon’s minimum perigee and Kipchoge’s record marathon time, then I’ll compute distance ÷ pace and round to the nearest 1000 hours. I’m retrieving the relevant Wikipedia data first.


I’m searching Wikipedia for the Moon and Eliud Kipchoge entries.
```python
wiki_search = await wikipedia_search("Moon Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record", max_results=5)
print(wiki_search)
```

The first search did not expose usable result text, so I’m querying the two Wikipedia topics separately to obtain the exact figures.
```python
moon_search = await wikipedia_search("Moon", max_results=3)
print(moon_search)
```

```python
source_search = await web_search("Wikipedia Moon minimum perigee Eliud Kipchoge marathon record pace", max_results=5)
print(source_search)
```
I have the needed inputs from the reference pages: minimum lunar perigee 356400 km and Kipchoge’s 2:01:09 marathon record. I’m calculating the equivalent travel time and applying the requested rounding.
```python
time_hours = await calculator("356400 / (42.195 / (2 + 1/60 + 9/3600))")
print(time_hours)
```
17000 hours
